title: Continuous microfluidic synthesis of zirconium-based UiO-67 using a coiled flow invertor reactor
author: Bailey, Pinto, et al.

steps.title: Heat CFIR to target temperature
steps.instruction: Place the coiled flow invertor reactor (CFIR) in an oil bath and heat the bath to 140 °C using a magnetic stirrer hotplate.

steps.title: Prepare zirconium precursor solution
steps.instruction: In a dry beaker combine 0.26 mmol ZrCl₄ and 1.28 mmol benzoic acid, add 10 mL DMF (initial small amount to capture HCl gas), sonicate 1 min; then add 0.26 mmol BPDC and 0.25 mL distilled water, sonicate an additional 3 min.

substeps.instruction: Add ZrCl₄ (0.26 mmol) and benzoic acid (1.28 mmol) to a dry beaker.
Add DMF (10 mL) – the initial small volume helps absorb HCl released from ZrCl₄.
Sonicate the mixture for 1 minute.
Add BPDC (0.26 mmol) and distilled water (0.25 mL).
Sonicate the resulting solution for 3 minutes.

steps.title: Load solution into stir‑bar syringe
steps.instruction: Using a 10 mL syringe that contains a small magnetic stir bar, draw up the entire reactant solution.

steps.title: Flush microreactor with fresh DMF
steps.instruction: Quickly pump 2 mL fresh DMF through the CFIR (internal volume 1.72 mL) to remove any residual material before attaching the reaction syringe.

steps.title: Connect syringe and start reaction flow
steps.instruction: Attach the loaded syringe to the microreactor, place the syringe on the pump, and set a small magnetic stir plate above the syringe.

substeps.instruction: Connect the syringe to the CFIR via the IDEX flangeless fittings and threaded luer adapters.
Position a magnetic stir plate beneath the syringe to keep the internal stir bar moving.

steps.title: Run reaction for specified duration
steps.instruction: Set the pump flow rate to 0.052 mL min⁻¹ (giving a 30 min residence time) and run the reaction for 2.5 h; the magnetic stir bar will stop spinning after this period.

substeps.instruction: Program the pump to 0.052 mL min⁻¹.
Run the flow for 2.5 hours (residence time ≈30 min).
Monitor the magnetic stir bar; it stops after the 2.5 h run.

steps.title: Post‑reaction flushing of reactor
steps.instruction: Replace the reaction syringe with a new syringe containing 5 mL fresh DMF, then push 2 mL DMF at 0.052 mL min⁻¹ followed by another 2 mL DMF at 1 mL min⁻¹ to evacuate all product and reactants.

substeps.instruction: Attach a fresh 5 mL DMF‑filled syringe to the CFIR.
Pump 2 mL DMF at the same flow rate (0.052 mL min⁻¹) to match the residence time.
Pump an additional 2 mL DMF at 1 mL min⁻¹ to clear any settled material.

steps.title: Wash and soak product in solvents
steps.instruction: Collect the product and wash it with fresh DMF (2 × 15 mL); then soak the washed solid in 15 mL methanol for 72 h, replacing the methanol every 24 h.

substeps.instruction: Wash the solid with 15 mL DMF, discard, then repeat for a second 15 mL DMF wash.
Transfer the washed solid to 15 mL methanol and let stand for 72 hours.
Replace the methanol with fresh methanol every 24 hours (three total exchanges).

steps.title: Centrifuge and dry product
steps.instruction: After each solvent removal, centrifuge the sample at 6000 rpm for 20 minutes, then dry the solid overnight in an oven set to 110 °C.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 6000 rpm for 20 min to remove solvent.
Place the pellet in an oven at 110 °C and dry overnight.

steps.title: Perform PXRD and SEM analysis
steps.instruction: Analyze the dried UiO‑67 by powder X‑ray diffraction (2θ = 5°–45°, 45 min scan, 0.033° interval, Cu Kα radiation) and by scanning electron microscopy using a Carl Zeiss EVO MA15 after sputter‑coating with 25 nm iridium.

substeps.instruction: PXRD: scan from 2θ = 5° to 45°, total time 45 min, step size 0.033°, Cu Kα source.
SEM: sputter‑coat the sample with 25 nm iridium, then image using a Carl Zeiss EVO MA15.
